name: Draining HP bar
oneLiner: A hit drops the fill at once while a pale loss segment holds where the health was, then drains down; quick hits extend the hold and merge into one segment, a heal shows a mint gain segment before the fill rises, and low health pulses. One module draws the framed boss bar, the party HUD bars and the small over-head bars in world space, smooth on HD canvases and crisp whole-pixel bars on native pixel canvases. It watches the HP the game already has: set(id, hp, max) every step, the curves are parameters and readable from state().
fits: platformer and metroidvania (boss and player bars)
notFor: damage numbers over units (use C-11 / E-01)
resource bars that refill constantly (stamina, mana regen): use a plain gauge, the loss segment would never settle
games that show health as hearts or pips (no continuous bar)

needs: each unit's current HP and max HP, read every fixed step (no hook into the damage code)
a stable id per unit for its whole life
the places that create or refill units (new game, battle, wave, respawn) to snap without animation
the rects where the game draws its HP bars now (HUD in screen space, over-head bars inside the camera transform)
provides: drawn boss, party and over-head HP bars with loss / gain segments, hit flash, shake and low-HP pulse
state(id) and curve(id): hp, fill, gain top, loss top and phase per step, for tests and judges
shown(id): a rolling HP number that agrees with the bar
debug events (track, damage, merge, drain, drained, heal, fill, filled, reset)

assets: module/draining-hp-bar.js: the element as one dependency-free script (global GameDNA_DrainingHpBar): the HP model (fill, gain top, loss top, hold, merge, cap, drain and fill tweens), boss / party / unit bar drawing in smooth and crisp modes, a built-in 3x5 bitmap font for crisp labels and numbers
no image, font or audio files (system sans stack, never loaded from the network)
